proposals.question: What do AI developers' own safety evaluations leave unmeasured, and what would an independent record of dangerous AI behaviour need before anyone looks?
proposals.docks_onto: Cycle 006 found every stand-in for the missing record kept by the party the claim concerns: of 14 incidents of AI pursuing its own goals, 8 were first seen by the developer and 0 under a rule published before the looking.

proposals.question: Who can witness what AI systems do, under a rule written before the looking and not by their makers, and what would make a maker testify against itself?
proposals.docks_onto: Cycle 006 found every stand-in for AI-extinction evidence kept by the party it concerns (0 of 14 incidents seen under a prior rule; markets settled by the accused), so it asks what witness could be built now.

proposals.question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
proposals.docks_onto: Cycle 006 found that an AI extinction can only ever be written NO and that each of its stand-ins is kept by someone who must outlive it; a near miss is the one record of catastrophe the living can keep, so its keepers can be studied.

findings.line: The evidence on AI and extinction is produced by the parties it concerns; the missing datum that could exist is an observer who fixed the recording rule before looking.
every stand-in for the record an extinction cannot leave is kept by someone who must outlive it; ask of any evidence who would be left to write its other answer.
When an outcome can never be observed, each stand-in for it (who answered, what can be paid out, what is scored) rewards something other than being right about the world.
